name: neural_te
notes: The row 16 embedding MLP on the target-encoded features. One variable against row 16: identical architecture, hyperparameters, folds, seed and early-stopping rule (512/256/128, BatchNorm, SiLU, 0.2 dropout, 8-dim embeddings, AdamW under OneCycle, 30 epochs, patience 5, batch 4096); only the feature set changes, the numeric block going from 9 raw + 9 mask to 33 (9 raw + 24 encoded) + 9 mask. Encoder fingerprinted against 13 and identical (0642e41750ef8bab), fit inside the fold loop, with the quantile transform and median imputation also fit on training rows only inside the same loop. Kaggle T4, 16.1 min, fold alignment verified on all five checks. Paired vs row 16 +0.026204, sd 0.000568, 5/5 folds, t=103. THE >2% RULE IN CLAUDE.md FIRED AT +2.7901% AND WAS INVESTIGATED RATHER THAN CELEBRATED. Not a leak, and the argument is that the new number is BELOW both GBDTs on the identical encoder (row 17 LightGBM 0.966782, row 26 CatBoost 0.966915), while 13's deliberate no-nesting sanity check scores 0.9967, so a leaking encoder is loud here and three LB-confirmed models already use this exact one. Leak checks reproduce 13's numbers exactly (validation 0.0, training 8.130e-05 against a prior shift of 1.302e-04) and row 16's own vector reproduces its ledger CV to -8.36e-08, so the baseline is right too. The rule fired because the DENOMINATOR was weak, not because the numerator is anomalous. The neural model goes from 0.0247 behind the best GBDT to 0.0015 behind. Spearman 0.9826 vs row 17 and 0.9757 vs row 26, the latter near the bottom of the 0.9741 to 0.9981 band LightGBM produces against itself, so it is still differently wrong while now being strong. Not submitted on its own; the decision is what a fitted combiner does with it, which is row 34. The notebook header predicted an MLP would gain little from a representation that only removes a many-splits cost trees were paying. That prediction was recorded before the run and was wrong by a wide margin.

name: stack_logit_24_oof
notes: Row 32's stack with neural_te added as a twenty-fourth member. One variable against row 32: same combiner, same C, same fold-wise protocol, same folds; only the member set changes, 23 to 24. The old raw-feature neural model is KEPT rather than replaced, since removing it would make this two variables. Row 32 is refit in the same run and reproduces its recorded CV to +1.30e-08. Paired vs row 32 +0.000043, sd 0.000016, 5/5 folds, t(4)=5.84. Real, and small: three times the last CatBoost-seed addition (+0.000014) but under half the original CatBoost addition (+0.000100), against a single-model improvement of +0.026204. THE COEFFICIENTS ARE THE RESULT, NOT THE CV. neural_te takes +0.1305, the largest positive weight in the whole 24-member stack, above every GBDT in it. The old neural model does NOT collapse: it goes from +0.1181 to +0.0905, keeping 77 percent of its weight, so the two neural models are wrong in different directions FROM EACH OTHER as well as from the trees, rather than being one mechanism at two strengths. The weight neural_te takes comes mostly out of the GBDTs, with the five CatBoost coefficients falling from +0.4016 to +0.3212 and the TE seeds dropping in step. WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT STACKING: a 0.026 single-model gain bought 0.000043 in the stack, because the weak neural model at +0.118 was already supplying most of the neural direction and the combiner only needed a cleaner version of a signal it already had. Spearman of the test ordering against the submitted row 32 is 0.9998335, so the leaderboard cannot resolve this and it is not worth a slot over row 32; it is however the CV-best row in the file and therefore a final-selection candidate. Run locally by nbconvert --execute on a clean kernel, notebooks/22_stack_24.ipynb, outputs kept in the notebook as the run record.

name: stack_logit_24_pruned

Row 44 is refit in the same run and reproduces its recorded CV to +1.23e-07. The first experiment in this competition that makes the stack smaller. The removal set was chosen by reading row 44's coefficients off this same out-of-fold matrix, which is selection on the validation set, the error this repo refused to commit when it kept seed 2024 in the raw-feature blend. The notebook pre-registered a check that the drop be supported by training-fold information alone, and it failed: the largest coefficient a dropped member reached in a training-fold fit was +0.0193, above the +0.0051 threshold the check compared it against. THE CHECK WAS MIS-SPECIFIED AND THAT IS MY ERROR, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE DATA. It compared a MAX over five folds for the dropped members against a MEAN over five folds for the kept members, which is not like for like, and a single-fold maximum will exceed a mean almost by construction. The verdict stands as written rather than being rerun with a friendlier rule, because moving a pre-registered bar after seeing the number is the failure the bar exists to prevent. Selection bias here can only inflate the pruned stack, since the members were chosen for looking useless on these rows. XGBoost has taken their role. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DONE WITH IT: nothing. Row 44 stays the selection candidate. Spearman between the two is 0.9999992, so they are the same submission, and simplicity alone does not justify acting against a pre-registered discard. name: xgb_smooth1
notes: One variable against row 38: the encoder's smoothing constant. Same learner, same folds, same seed 42, same budget, same N_INNER=5; only SMOOTH moves. The encoder source is untouched and still fingerprints 0642e41750ef8bab, because _stats reads SMOOTH from module globals, so each arm rebinds the constant and calls the same function. A live-constant check ran before the sweep and confirmed SMOOTH reaches the encoder (0.366 largest change in an encoded column between 10 and 100); without it five identical arms would have produced a perfectly flat curve, which is exactly the result the header predicted, and the coincidence would have been indistinguishable from success. Kaggle CPU, 25 encoder builds. Leak checks PASS, fold alignment verified, determinism OK, and the SMOOTH=10 arm reproduces row 38 to -1.46e-07. Not submitted, not carried forward. THE POINT OF THE SWEEP: SMOOTH was written into cell 1 of 13_target_encoding.ipynb on 2026-08-11, chosen once, and 22 of the 29 members of row 44 inherited it without it ever being varied. It was the last untested constant in the pipeline. NULL, AND THE PREDICTION HELD. The curve is flat from 1 to 10, where 1.0 and 5.0 sit +0.000023 and +0.000017 above the baseline on 3 of 5 folds, which is a coin flip, and it falls above 10, at -0.000062 (0/5) for 25 and -0.000219 (0/5) for 100. SMOOTH=10 sits on the flat part. The header predicted this from the arithmetic: at roughly 500 rows per level the shrinkage toward the prior is about 2 percent, so the constant is close to inert by construction, and the grid ran to 100 to confirm the flat part was actually being left before calling it flat. WHAT IT CONFIRMS BEYOND ITSELF: this is the fifth reopening measured in this repo and the pattern recorded after num_leaves now has five points. The three that paid changed the LEARNER or its input (CatBoost row 26, the neural model row 33, XGBoost row 38). The two that returned nothing changed a HYPERPARAMETER of a component already fitted to the representation (num_leaves rows 35 to 37, SMOOTH here). A change of representation revalues learners, not their knobs.

name: xgb_inner2
notes: Arm N_INNER=2, paired -0.000162 vs the base arm, sd 0.000087, 0/5 folds. The only arm that loses on every fold, so the curve does have a falling side and the flat part is genuinely being left. One variable against row 38 (xgb_te, 0.967099): the target encoder's inner split count N_INNER, the number of folds used to build TRAINING-row encodings. Same learner, same outer folds, same seed, same budget, same SMOOTH=10.0, same encoder source (fingerprint 0642e41750ef8bab, matches 13). The last constant in this pipeline that had never been varied: 13_target_encoding.ipynb set it to 5 on 2026-08-11 and 22 of row 44's 29 members inherited it. THE ARM AT N_INNER=5 REPRODUCES ROW 38 AT -1.46e-07, which is the tightest reproduction in this repo. Fold alignment verified against sha ec282b0968059676, leak checks pass, determinism exact. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS TWO-SIDED AND BOTH SIDES FIRED. N_INNER is read only by the inner out-of-fold pass, so it must move training-row encodings and must leave validation-row encodings bit-identical. Measured before any model trained: train moved 1.637e-01, validation moved exactly 0. Notebook 29's control could only check the first of those, because SMOOTH reaches every column. SWEEP RESULT, NULL. Arms 2/3/5/10/20 give 0.966937/0.967016/0.967099/0.967107/0.967096. Flat at and above 5, falling below it. The best arm is N_INNER=10 at +0.000009 paired, 2/5 folds, which is not paired-significant and is 11x under the +0.00010 gate floor pre-registered in the header. THE HEADER'S ALTERNATIVE MECHANISM WAS PREDICTED AND REFUTED. Training rows are encoded from (N_INNER-1)/N_INNER of the fold while validation rows are encoded from all of it, a real train/serve mismatch that a larger N_INNER narrows, so the header predicted a curve rising monotonically toward 20. It does not rise: 10 is +0.000009 and 20 is -0.000003, both inside noise. The mismatch is real and worth nothing, which is the same shape as the decimal lattice in row 19. SIXTH POINT ON THE RULE IN NOTES.md, and it is the second knob to return nothing on this representation after num_leaves and SMOOTH. Three learner reopenings paid, three hyperparameter sweeps did not. Kaggle Save and Run All, vyask21/smartphone-addiction-inner version 1, 36m 28s, notebooks/30_inner_splits.ipynb.

The bench compared a 100-iteration model against a 200-iteration model sliced to 100, which straddles that threshold, so they are different model families and the check was right to refuse. Sweeping iterations on default CatBoost is therefore NOT a one-variable experiment: it moves the budget, the leaf estimation and the depth of category combinations together, with no warning. Version 2 pins both at the values CatBoost picks at 2,000 iterations, which is what row 70 ran, so iterations is genuinely the only variable here. notes: LightGBM, no encoder, ratio block ON. One variable against row 68 (lgb_raw, 0.963464): +0.000356, sd 0.000472, 4/5 folds, t(4)=1.69. All pure functions of other feature columns, asserted bit-identical under a permutation of y. Added RAW, not target encoded, since encoding them would be a second variable. missing_count deliberately EXCLUDED although the public recipes carry it, because 04_missingness_diagnostic.ipynb measured missingness here as a null: no feature shows a target-rate lift outside sampling error when missing and a row's missing count correlates +0.0025 with the target. Encoder fingerprint 0642e41750ef8bab for the encoded arm, leak checks reproduce 13's numbers exactly, determinism exact on all four arms. THE GENERATOR FINGERPRINT IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN CITATION: on 421,427 complete rows, 0.0000 percent violate daily >= social + gaming + work_study, median slack +0.750 h. A hard floor the source file does not have. THE 2 BY 2 REFUTED THE PREDICTION, AND THAT IS THE RESULT. The header predicted positive on the three no-encoder views (+0.001 to +0.003) and null or negative on the encoded arm (-0.0005 to +0.0005), reasoning that 24 encoded columns already price what a ratio carries. The views came in at a mean of +0.000522, BELOW the predicted band, and the encoded arm came in at +0.000906, the LARGEST gain of the four and well above its predicted band. The difference runs -0.000384 the wrong way. The ratio block is not redundant with target encoding; it is worth MORE alongside it. WHAT THAT OVERTURNS. NOTES.md has explained rows 18 and 19 since 2026-08-12 with the general claim that a block measured on top of full target encoding comes back null because the encoder already extracts what it carries. As a general claim that is now false. It may still be the right account of imputed copies and the decimal lattice specifically, which are the two things rows 18 and 19 actually tested and which are both deterministic functions of a SINGLE column. A ratio is not: it is a function of TWO columns, and 1-way target encoding cannot represent it at any smoothing. HOW THIS RECONCILES WITH ROW 32, which found crossed pair encodings worth nothing. Both a ratio and a crossed cell inject 2-way information, and row 31 established that real 2-way structure exists. They differ in FORM. name: xgb_bin256
notes: The default and row 93's value, so this arm is the reproduction check rather than a treatment. -3.10e-07 against row 93. One variable against row 93 (xgb_te_fe, 0.968005): XGBoost's max_bin. Same 49 features, same encoder fingerprinted 0642e41750ef8bab, same ratio block, same folds, same seed, same budget, same depth. Leak checks pass, determinism exact on every arm, the 256 arm reproduces row 93 at -3.10e-07. THE RESULT IS NULL AND MY PREDICTION WAS WRONG BY MORE THAN AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. The header predicted +0.0010 to +0.0030 landing between 0.9690 and 0.9710. The best arm is 1536 at +0.000049, 5/5 folds but t(4)=3.45, and 3072 falls back to +0.000009. kito_pl measured +0.0023 from this same setting on the same fold split. We got a fortieth of it. WHY THE PUBLIC NUMBER DOES NOT TRANSFER, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT I WROTE DOWN AND THEN TALKED MYSELF OUT OF. The first draft of the header predicted UNDER kito_pl on the grounds that our encoder and ratio block already recover per-value structure by other means. The smoke run then showed 27 of 49 columns exceed 256 distinct values, I read that as evidence the compression was worse than I thought, and I widened the band upward. The cardinality was real and the inference from it was wrong: what matters is not how many distinct values get compressed, it is whether anything the model needs is lost when they are. TARGET ENCODING AND max_bin ARE SUBSTITUTES, NOT COMPLEMENTS. Both recover the same thing, the per-value lookup structure this generator produces. The encoder hands the model a smoothed per-level target statistic directly; fine bins let the binner isolate the value so the tree can find it itself. Do the first and the second has nothing left to add. kito_pl's baseline had no target encoding, which is exactly why their number is large and ours is not. THIS RETRACTS A CLAIM I MADE ON 2026-08-22 AND ROW 19 STANDS AS WRITTEN. Earlier today I argued that NOTES.md's explanation of row 19 had a hole: that te_weekend_screen_time inherits about 1,459 distinct values, gets bucketed to 256, and therefore the decimal-lattice signal had never reached a model. That was a real, testable claim and this run tests it. It is false. name: neural_fixed
notes: Row 33's architecture with the epoch-selection rule removed. One variable against row 33 (neural_te, 0.965373): the selection rule. Same 512/256/128 network, same 8-dim categorical embeddings, same BatchNorm, SiLU and 0.2 dropout, same AdamW under OneCycle, same 30 epochs, same batch 4096, same folds, same seed, same encoder. Row 33's own vector re-scores here at +3.10e-08. WHY THIS ARM EXISTS: rows 16 and 33 keep the best-validation-AUC epoch and then report that fold's AUC, so the model is selected on the fold it is scored on. The ledger records the rule but never that it is optimistic, and 35_native_catboost.ipynb had criticised public notebooks for exactly this. Both rows are live members, neural_te carrying +0.0717 and neural +0.0038 in row 94. THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG IN SIGN, AND I HAD WRITTEN THAT THE SIGN WAS NOT IN DOUBT. The header predicted neural_fixed would land 0.0003 to 0.0015 BELOW row 33, on the grounds that selecting the best of 30 epochs on the scored fold cannot be pessimistic. It lands 0.000029 ABOVE it, losing only 1 of 5 folds. THE REASON IS THAT PATIENCE CUTS BOTH WAYS AND I ONLY COUNTED ONE SIDE. Row 33 used patience 5. The validation curve on this architecture rises monotonically all the way to epoch 29 in every fold, from about 0.9536 at epoch 0 to 0.9648 to 0.9658 at the end, with the last five epochs still worth +0.0003. So a patience counter on a slowly rising curve fires on a plateau and TRUNCATES training, and that truncation costs more than the selection bias gains. The bias is real; it is just smaller than the damage done by the mechanism that creates it. WHAT THIS SETTLES: rows 16 and 33 are NOT materially optimistic, the 41-member stack CV in row 94 is not inflated by them, and no member vector needs regenerating before final selection. That was the question worth asking with nine days left, and the answer is that nothing is broken. This arm is NOT added to the stack. name: neural_lookup
notes: neural_fixed plus a per-value embedding table for each of the nine numeric columns. One variable against neural_fixed, measured in the same kernel: one embedding table per numeric column keyed on the EXACT value, 8 dimensions, about 39,000 new parameters over 691,369 rows. DECISIVELY NEGATIVE: paired -0.004221 against neural_fixed, sd 0.000241, 0/5 folds, t(4)=-39.21, the most decisive single arm in this ledger in either direction. THE MECHANISM IS VISIBLE IN THE TRAINING CURVE AND IT IS MEMORISATION. Every fold peaks near epoch 10 at about 0.9645 and then declines monotonically to about 0.9612 by epoch 29, while the arm WITHOUT the embeddings rises monotonically to the end. The embedding tables give each of roughly 5,500 distinct values eight free parameters, each value is seen about 100 times in a training fold, and the network spends the back half of the schedule memorising them. Even taken at its epoch-10 peak, before the decline, it is still below neural_fixed's 0.965402. THIS IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT ROUTE TO PER-VALUE STRUCTURE THAT PAYS NOTHING ON TOP OF THE ENCODER, and the three together are now a finding rather than three nulls. Row 19 gave the trees the first decimal digit: -0.000132. Rows 101 to 105 gave the binner six times the resolution: +0.000049. This gives a network a free parameter vector per value: -0.004221. Target encoding already prices what a value is worth, and every attempt to supply the same information by another route is at best redundant and at worst an invitation to overfit. THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG AGAIN, AND THE CASE-AGAINST WAS RIGHT AGAIN. The header predicted -0.0005 to +0.0025 and the answer is -0.004221, outside the band. The header ALSO contained a section headed 'the honest case against, and it is strong' which argued from the max_bin result that a third route to the same information should be redundant. That section was correct. The same thing happened in row 42, where the case-against was right and the prediction was wrong, and in row 39, where the case-against named the exact mechanism. Across three runs my case-against sections have outperformed my predictions, which is a strange and useful thing to have measured about my own reasoning: I am better at arguing against an idea I want to work than at pricing it. IT STILL GOES TO THE GATE. The header committed to that in advance, and the 2026-08-12 correction stands: row 96 added a model 0.0033 weaker than the stack it joined and fired at 5/5 folds. A model that is wrong in a NEW way can be worth weight, and an overfit-to-values model is wrong in a way nothing else here is. Membership is a separate row. notes: TabM, our implementation of Gorishniy et al's parameter-efficient ensembling: one shared weight matrix per layer plus a per-member rank-1 adapter, so K=32 members train JOINTLY inside one network against a shared backbone. NOT one variable against anything, it is a new model in the sense row 135 was. What is held is the data: same folds, same encoder 0642e41750ef8bab, same 13-column ratio block, same median/IQR/smooth-clip preprocessing, same 55 numeric columns, same masks. Deliberately plain schedule, no EMA, no label smoothing, no parameter-group multipliers, so the class is not confounded with RealMLP's tricks. 14.6 min on a T4. Paired -0.000962 against row 138 at 0/5 folds, reported as context rather than as a controlled test since architecture and schedule both differ. Fourth best single model here, behind xgb_tuned 0.968222, cat_te_fe 0.968036 and realmlp10 0.967892, and well clear of the 0.966 cliff. THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS THE CORRELATION AND IT IS BAD: Spearman 0.991615 against realmlp10, 0.990503 against realmlp, 0.990126 against xgb_tuned, 0.990399 against cat_te_fe. That sits INSIDE this repo's within-family band of 0.9741 to 0.9981, so TabM is no more different from RealMLP than two members of one family are from each other. THE CASE AGAINST WAS RIGHT AGAIN, ninth time in eleven, and it was specific: the header said 'if TabM lands at Spearman 0.99 against realmlp10 this is row 139 again and returns nothing'. It landed at 0.9916. THE FINDING: this is the THIRD time reasoning from a distinct mechanism to decorrelated errors has failed here. CatBoost's ordered target statistics predicted disagreement that did not appear (0.9877). logit_te_fe was decorrelated at 0.9227 and took coefficient -0.0007. TabM trains its members jointly rather than independently, which IS a different object from RealMLP's internal averaging, and it makes the same errors anyway. A new mechanism is not a new direction. The real cost was 14.6 min, because the K dimension batches into one matmul and keeps the GPU busy rather than costing K times the wall clock. The width cut was therefore unnecessary and this row understates what a faithful TabM would score. Not submitted, membership is row 144.
